sentences.text: This part adds up the daytime and evening charges and night-time minutes for customers with few voice-mail messages, and acts on 661 of 4000 training customers, 267 of whom left; for the typical customer it acts on, the chance of leaving is about 27% without it and about 82% with it.

Through it, the daytime charge adds nothing until about 39.93 US dollars (between 32.28 and 53.10 US dollars for different customers), then raises the chance in an uneven way: for a typical customer from about 12% to about 81%, flattening out near the top because the predicted chance cannot go much higher.

The daytime charge raises it, in an uneven way, only for customers with no voice-mail messages (from about 12% to about 43%, against about 40% throughout otherwise), and more so with an evening charge above 17.12 US dollars (about 12% to about 72%, against about 12% to about 16%).

For the typical customer it acts on, a higher evening charge (about 27% to about 95%) and more night-time minutes (about 42% to about 93%) raise it in an uneven way, flattening out near the top because the predicted chance cannot go much higher, while more voice-mail messages lower it in an uneven way, from about 82% to about 27%.

sentences.label: Plans
sentences.text: An international plan raises a typical customer's chance of leaving from about 12% to about 65%, a voice-mail plan lowers it to about 2%, and more voice-mail messages raise it steadily, from about 12% at 0 to about 44% at 32 messages.

sentences.text: Each extra international call lowers it by about the same amount (about 14% at 2 to about 9% at 8 calls), more evening minutes lower it steadily (about 13% at 138 to about 10% at 266 minutes), and a longer account raises it steadily (about 11% at 48 to about 13% at 152).

Together they add nothing until about 3 calls (between 2 and 3 calls for different customers), then raise the chance in an uneven way: going from 0 to 4 calls takes a typical customer from about 12% to about 36%.

parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: churn logit = -2.164 + linearBackbone + 2.82*heavyUsageNoVmail + serviceCalls + intlChargeHinges + stateUnits + accountLengthHinge, an additive (parallel) composition in the output pre-activation; output = sigmoid. 25 unconnected inputs (incl. totalDayCalls, totalEveCalls, totalIntlMinutes, totalNightCharge, area codes and 17 states) are zero-effect entries. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000, local ablation): full AUC 0.9243 (L2 logistic regression 0.8433). All nonlinear children jointly replaced by least-squares linear fits on their own inputs: 0.8333; all hidden mean-ablated: 0.659. The 0.091 nonlinear gain comes from two children: heavyUsageNoVmail (restore alone +0.0708, Shapley 0.057) and serviceCalls (+0.0489, Shapley 0.035); restoring both gives 0.9244 (= full). intlChargeHinges, stateUnits and accountLengthHinge contribute nothing over their linear fits. The model is miscalibrated on train (mean p 0.336 vs base rate 0.1415; global shift -1.875 needed). Rare-category effects are constant offsets: state:11 -2.18, state:46 -1.63, state:4 +1.12 (mixed direct/hidden, range -0.53..+1.48), state:47 +0.92, state:39 -0.86, state:31 +0.70, state:45 off-switch of the call veto.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
